title: Served price by state (SPEC-ORC-017): fresh when Live, fresh when Drifting without disagreement, min(lower, fresh) during a disagreement, A when Cached, 1 when Expired; served >= 1 always, <= A whenever failed, <= fresh whenever not failed (even when the floored lower exceeds fresh), <= price8 of getTokenPrices() and equal to it when Live, Cached or Drifting without disagreement; the accepted price and checkpoint stay >= 1 after every poke

The accepted price changes only from a Live observation newer than the stored one; its timestamp never decreases and is a source timestamp; re-reading the same rounds never refreshes it; the served timestamp is a source timestamp (accepted when failed, the routes in use otherwise)
expiredLatched is set only when source timestamps show Expired; a caught error, a config/decimals failure or a gas shortfall never sets it, and a gas-short poke changes nothing
poke() is idempotent within a block: a second poke on the same reads changes no stored field (timers, latch, recoveredAt, accepted price, checkpoint)

After a poke a disagreeing market is Drifting, served at min(lower, fresh) and liquidation-paused; the first-observation time is set once per episode (per route version) and never moves; the pause lasts < disagreementPauseMax from it, then disagreementExpired holds until the routes agree
No stored timer, latch or route version keeps a market out of Live once its inputs are valid, fresh and agree; a failed market is Expired at most cachedWindow after its failure start

Cached window (SPEC-ORC-013): Cached is never reported at or after min(F + H, S_ts) + cachedWindow, F the true failure start and H the keeper poke interval; once a poke saw the recovery, Expired is never reported before F + cachedWindow; a stored failedSince only brings Expired earlier, and later failed pokes never move it

A grace window started by the latch fallback recoveredAt = min(newest leg in use, now) never starts after the poke's block and, when the recovered route's timestamp is its new round, never before the recovery; the REQ-ORACLE-032 example gives grace until 1,762,651,800

The latch fallback never starts a grace window before the recovery, also when the recovered token is on a two-leg route or recovered through a standby switch (REQ-ORACLE-032: 'The window must start no earlier than the recovery')
detail: REQ-ORACLE-032 examples: a two-leg recovery (new USDT/ETH round 1,762,700,000, ETH/USD 1,762,697,000, token0 1,762,696,500) gives recoveredAt 1,762,700,000; a standby switched in at 1,762,700,000 and observed by the poke at 1,762,700,012 gives recoveredAt 1,762,700,012.

title: REQ-ORACLE-032 examples: two-leg recovery (USDT/ETH 1,762,700,000, ETH/USD 1,762,697,000, token0 1,762,696,500, poke 1,762,700,060) gives recoveredAt 1,762,700,000 and grace until 1,762,701,800 (route timestamps would give 1,762,697,000); standby switch observed at 1,762,700,012 gives recoveredAt 1,762,700,012 and grace until 1,762,701,812 (newest leg 1,762,698,000 would end grace at 1,762,699,800, before the poke)

now - servedUpdatedAt <= borrowPriceMaxAge() (resp. liquidationPriceMaxAge()) holds exactly when every leg in use is within its own borrow (resp. liquidation, alternates held to min(liq, borrow)) limit; both derived limits are never negative

For every combination of leg behaviours (10^4 cases x gas x Cached/Expired) latestAnswer() returns a value >= 1 (1 exactly when Expired, <= A when not Live), and reverts only with InsufficientGas after a caught failure below pokeMinGas
price8 = isqrt(4 v0 v1) - 1 is >= 1, (price8 + 1)^2 <= 4 v0 v1 (never above 2*sqrt(v0 v1)), within 2 units of it, and 4 v0 v1 < 2^256
The stable ceiling never raises a price, is monotone, and is a no-op at or below the ceiling

The agreement check |p - b| * 10^4 <= T * min(p, b) is symmetric in p and b (both sides are order-free) and uses no division; the SPEC-ORC-003 examples agree (b = 99,900,000) and disagree (b = 97,500,000) at T = 225
Witness: floor division would admit T + 1 bps where the exact check refuses (why the cross-multiplied form is required)
The reference sqrt price never overflows and lies in [MIN_SQRT_RATIO, MAX_SQRT_RATIO) after clamping

Lower-route price (SPEC-ORC-017): with w_i = ceil_i(min(p_i, b_i)) when both routes are valid (else v_i), 1 <= w_i <= v_i, so w0 w1 <= v0 v1 and lower = isqrt(4 w0 w1) - 1 satisfies 1 <= lower <= fresh; served = min(lower, fresh) lies in [1, fresh]

SPEC-ORC-017 example (full-range USDC/USDT, spacing 1, d = 6): A = 199,980,000; token1 routes 100,000,000 / 97,500,000 give the composition (987,420, 1,012,739), lower = 197,483,855 and served min(197,483,855, 199,999,600) = 197,483,855; Cached serves 199,980,000; Expired serves 1; Drifting on a consistency deviation with fresh 199,999,600 (both tokens at $1) serves 199,999,600, above A, and a top-up there is booked at min(199,999,600, 199,980,000) = 199,980,000

Whenever some token disagrees (REQ-ORACLE-008) and the market is not failed, pauseActive or disagreementExpired holds, so the market is served at min(lower, fresh) and liquidationPaused is true (REQ-ORACLE-086: 'While some token disagrees (SPEC-ORC-016 pauseActive or disagreementExpired)')
detail: Includes disagreementPauseMax = 0 (allowed: the bound is <= 3,600) with disagreeSince read as 0 (no poke yet in the episode, or a route-version change since the last poke): s = now, so disagreementExpired = D and now >= now + 0 holds.

title: Expired serves exactly 1 (REQ-ORACLE-085) and Cached serves A; whenever the served price is one of the stress values (Cached A, Expired 1, a disagreement's min(lower, fresh)), liquidationPaused is true, so no stress value sizes a seizure of this market: with liquidationPaused false the served price is exactly fresh

USD band: when both tokens are stables v0 v1 <= 10^16 < usdBandHigh^2, so only the uncapped lower bound can trip and a stable premium never breaches; testing capped values never breaches where uncapped would not; examples: GHO 104,700,000 with USDC 1e8 is in band (uncapped it would breach), 99,987,000 x 100,010,000 in band, both at 89,000,000 breach low

Feed age rules: borrowPriceMaxAge = min(hb + 600, 4,200) is at most 4,200 and at most liquidationPriceMaxAge; for every primary or standby leg (hb <= 3,600) it equals hb + 600, so a feed whose next round comes at most hb + d after the last (d < 600 s network delay) is never refused by the borrow age

Witness: the REQ-CONFIG-023 examples are admissible: USDC/USD hb 3,600 (borrow 4,200, feedMaxAge = liquidation 4,200) and a USDC/ETH alternate leg hb 86,400 (borrow 4,200, feedMaxAge = liquidation 87,000)

Alternates held to their borrow age: each leg's liquidation limit is >= its borrow limit (so borrowPriceMaxAge() <= liquidationPriceMaxAge()); while a serving alternate leg is past its borrowPriceMaxAge (ALTERNATE_PAST_BORROW_AGE) the liquidation age test already fails

SPEC-ORC-015 / REQ-ORACLE-090 examples: servedUpdatedAt 1,762,646,400, liquidation and borrow deadlines 1,762,650,600, both age limits 4,200 (own alternate limit would allow seizure until 1,762,733,400); with token1 back on its primary both deadlines 1,762,650,600; at 1,762,650,601 the USDT/ETH leg is 4,201 s old and ALTERNATE_PAST_BORROW_AGE is set

SPEC-ORC-013 examples: staleFrom 1,004,201 and 1,134,201 give staleAt 1,134,201, Cached until 1,137,800 and Expired from 1,137,801; a failedSince of 1,000,000 left by an unobserved recovery gives failureStart 1,000,000 at the poke at 1,004,100, Expired at once instead of Cached until 1,007,600

Phase rollover: with the fallback prev = seen.updatedAt <= the true previous round, every leg gap, route stale interval S_r and both-stale interval B_i contains the true one with the same end, so Expired-by-timestamps evidence is never lost on an aggregator upgrade, recoveredAt_new never decreases, and recoveredAt_new <= now

SPEC-ORC-014 examples: S_primary = [1,004,201, 1,200,000), alternate gap [1,134,201, 1,190,000), B lasts 55,799 s >= 3,600, recoveredAt = 1,190,000, graceEndsAt = 1,191,800; phase fallback from seen 996,400 gives [1,000,601, 1,200,000), which contains the true gap, and B is unchanged

A caught error never starts grace by itself: over every route outcome pair and latch origin, a grace window starts only from source timestamps (getRoundData, the previous-phase round, the oracle's own seen timestamp, staleFrom, or a latch set from timestamps); an unusable lookup or an Invalid/Error route gives no evidence

A route-version change changes only disagreeSince (now if some token disagrees, else 0) and, while latched and not failed, starts grace at recoveredAt = now (REQ-ORACLE-032 (a)); failedSince, expiredLatched, the accepted price and the checkpoint are as without the change, and recoveredAt too when not latched; the state is the same (never Live by itself); a failed market with failedSince != 0 is Expired from failedSince + cachedWindow whatever the new routes give; REQ-ORACLE-095 example: Expired from 1,762,653,600, disagreeSince 1,762,652,000
Witness (REQ-ORACLE-095 example): Cached with failedSince 1,762,650,000; a switch at 1,762,652,000 to a standby that disagrees with the alternate yields Drifting with disagreeSince 1,762,652,000

Failover and standby: over every primary/alternate/standby validity and slot, the quote is the primary slot when valid, else the alternate slot, else none; the standby in force is evaluated exactly as the route it replaces; every route in the primary slot has hourly legs (hb <= 3,600)

The checkpoint is written only by a poke with now >= checkpoint.at + 3,600, at block time, and always equals the accepted price after REQ-ORACLE-029 (never a stress-served price); a gas-short poke never writes it

Checkpoint example: (199,980,000, 1,762,650,000) is kept by a poke at 1,762,652,000 and replaced by (199,950,000, 1,762,653,700) at 1,762,653,700; 193,900,000 is 3.03 % below it and trips a 300 bps price-drop breaker until 1,762,660,900 (SPEC-BRK-001 compares while now - at <= 7,200)

DebtOracle (SPEC-ORC-018): served = q Live, max(p, b, A) disagreeing, A Cached, ceil(A(10^4 + delta)/10^4) Expired; served >= 1, served >= A whenever not Live, the Expired value is >= the exact rise, < exact + 1 and <= 1.5 A + 1, and A (10^4 + delta) < 2^256; liquidationPaused whenever not Live, so no stress value prices a repayment; accepted is written only when Live and newer; no stable ceiling (served = q above $1)
Witness: a Live debt asset above $1 is served uncapped (q = 100,300,000)

SPEC-ORC-018 examples: A = 99,990,000 Expired serves 104,989,500 at delta 500 (10,000 USDC of debt counts $10,498.95) and 101,989,800 at delta 200; A = 99,987,001 at delta 500 rounds 104,986,351.05 up to 104,986,352; routes 99,990,000 / 100,300,000 disagreeing with A = 99,995,000 serve 100,300,000; Cached serves 99,995,000

inGrace iff recoveredAt != 0 and recoveredAt <= now < recoveredAt + graceDuration: a grace window lasts exactly graceDuration seconds from recoveredAt, never before it, and a recoveredAt capped at now (SPEC-ORC-014, REQ-ORACLE-032) is in grace at the poke that sets it whenever graceDuration > 0
